crypto-macro.h3: Oil nears $100 as US-Iran strikes widen, hitting stocks, bonds and crypto
crypto-macro.summary: Brent crude climbed toward $100 a barrel on Tuesday 8 September after US forces hit Iran-linked tankers and Saudi energy sites came under attack, pushing the 10-year Treasury yield briefly above 4.8% and dragging equities and bitcoin lower.
body: CNBC reported that Brent for November delivery rose 2.2% to $99.16 on Tuesday while West Texas Intermediate gained 3.3% to $94.46, its highest in about three months, after attacks on Saudi Arabian energy facilities compounded fears of a wider confrontation between the United States and Iran. CBS News said American forces struck five oil tankers linked to Iran's Revolutionary Guards following attempted Iranian attacks on a US warship, while Iran-backed Houthi forces hit Saudi oil infrastructure and Riyadh retaliated in the worst exchange since the two sides agreed a truce four years ago.

Bloomberg noted that Iran said an agreement with Oman to manage shipping through the Strait of Hormuz was days away, which had limited the rally earlier in the session before the Saudi strikes changed the tone. Al Jazeera described Brent at a six to seven week high as traders weighed the risk of supply disruption against hopes for a shipping deal.

crypto-macro.h3: Markets lean toward a Fed hike as CPI looms before 15-16 Sept meeting
crypto-macro.summary: CME FedWatch pricing early in the week put the odds of a 25 basis point hike at the 15-16 September FOMC near 60%, with Friday's August CPI print the last big input.
body: Strong August payrolls of 162,000 with unemployment steady at 4.1% pushed hike odds up from the coin flip CNBC described in late August, as inflation stays above the 2% target and Chair Kevin Warsh has sounded hawkish. Prediction markets remain closer to even, with Polymarket and Kalshi showing hold and hike near 50-50.

Producer prices land Thursday and CPI Friday, and traders say either print could swing the narrow gap between hold and hike before the committee sits down next week. The oil spike from the Gulf conflict complicates the read, lifting headline inflation while weighing on growth.

crypto-macro.h3: ECB set to hike to 2.50% in Berlin on Thursday, Lagarde expected to stay vague
crypto-macro.summary: The European Central Bank meets on Thursday 10 September at the Bundesbank in Berlin, and markets on Tuesday priced a near-certain 25 basis point rise in the deposit rate to 2.50%, with attention on what President Lagarde signals for the path beyond.
body: Danske Bank's preview, published on FXStreet, expects a 25 basis point increase that takes the deposit rate to 2.50%, in line with consensus and market pricing. The analysts say the move has been telegraphed by Governing Council comments and the July minutes, with euro area headline inflation at 3.3%, growth near potential and inflation risks tilted upward.

The harder question is what comes next. Danske expects Lagarde to keep full optionality and avoid firm guidance, restating the reaction function rather than signalling a rate path. Short-term market pricing has moved sharply higher over the past month on renewed US-Iran tensions and now implies a peak deposit rate near 3.00% in 2027, a level the bank views as excessive but does not expect Lagarde to push back against.

crypto-macro.h3: Dow drops 1.2% in worst day in three weeks as yields and oil bite
crypto-macro.summary: US stocks fell on Tuesday 8 September, with the Dow losing 1.2%, the S&P 500 0.6% and the Nasdaq 0.3%, as crude approached $100 and the 10-year yield climbed to about 4.8% ahead of key inflation data.
body: CNBC's market coverage said the Dow posted its worst session in almost three weeks while the S&P 500 and Nasdaq Composite slid 0.6% and 0.3%. The 10-year Treasury yield briefly climbed above 4.8% during the day and ended around 4.796%, up 1.2 basis points, as rising oil prices added to inflation concerns.

Charles Schwab's market update pointed to three drivers: oil approaching $100 a barrel, an escalating US-Canada trade dispute after Ottawa's counter-tariffs took effect, and positioning ahead of inflation figures that could determine whether the Fed raises rates next week. The move in yields weighed on rate-sensitive sectors through the session.

crypto-macro.h3: Canada's $27.6 billion counter-tariffs on US goods take effect
crypto-macro.summary: Canadian retaliatory tariffs of 15% to 50% on $27.6 billion of American goods came into force at 12:01 a.m. on Tuesday 8 September, deepening a trade rift that has already pushed Ottawa to suspend talks with Washington.
body: CNBC reported that the duties cover hundreds of product categories including steel, aluminum and iron products, dairy, appliances, agricultural equipment, pulp and paper and electronics, with the highest 50% rate applied to US steel, aluminum, furniture and clothing. Canada's Department of Finance published the full list of affected products, saying the measures match Washington dollar for dollar.

The step responds to a 50% US tariff on $27.6 billion of Canadian goods that took effect on 22 August. Al Jazeera and NPR reported that Prime Minister Mark Carney suspended negotiations late last month after saying US negotiators introduced terms he called unfair, and described his country as being at war economically with the United States.

crypto-macro.h3: Yen hits seven-month high on BOJ hike bets, pressuring dollar and bitcoin
crypto-macro.summary: The Japanese yen rallied to its strongest level in nearly seven months on Tuesday 8 September as traders positioned for a Bank of Japan rate increase next week, with USD/JPY dipping below 153 before stabilising near 154.
body: Reuters, cited in CoinDesk's Daybook, reported that growing expectations of a BOJ rate hike next week sent bearish yen traders scrambling to cover, keeping the dollar subdued ahead of US inflation data. CoinDesk ran a live blog on Tuesday under the headline that the yen rally and rising bond yields were pressuring bitcoin and other risk assets.

FXStreet said USD/JPY touched a six-month low below 153.00 in Asian trade before rebounding to around 154.00 in the American session, describing the bounce as a technical correction. Upbeat Japanese wage growth figures and an upward revision to second-quarter GDP have cemented bets on a BOJ move at next week's meeting.

crypto-macro.h3: Bitcoin slips to $78,400 and ether holds near $2,470 as majors sell off
crypto-macro.summary: Bitcoin fell about 1.6% from Monday's open to roughly $78,400 on Tuesday 8 September, leaving it around 4% below last week's $82,320 high, while ether eased to about $2,470 and futures flow turned bearish on oil and Fed worries.
body: CoinDesk data showed bitcoin around $78,800 at midday, down 0.75% over 24 hours, before drifting toward $78,300 later in the session. Yahoo Finance said bitcoin opened at $79,094, 1.6% below Monday's open, and was at $78,371 by 7:20 a.m. ET. Ether opened at $2,490 and slipped to $2,474, while solana traded near $103.80. Over one month bitcoin is still up about 22% and ether about 30%, according to Yahoo Finance.

Derivatives positioning was cautious. CoinDesk reported the taker buy-sell ratio stayed bearish as tokens wilted under higher oil, Fed hike speculation and elevated yields. Open interest held around $141 billion while 24-hour volume rose 5% to $149.85 billion, suggesting churn rather than fresh leverage. Open interest in major USDT and USD bitcoin futures rose to 265,000 BTC from 257,000 BTC even as spot fell, which CoinDesk said pointed to some new shorts.

crypto-macro.h3: Spot bitcoin ETFs still $1 billion in the red for 2026 despite August surge
crypto-macro.summary: US spot bitcoin ETFs pulled in $3.52 billion in August and another $770 million in the first four sessions of September, yet CoinDesk calculated on Tuesday 8 September that year-to-date net flows remain about $1 billion negative.
body: CoinDesk's Omkar Godbole wrote that a spectacular August and a solid start to September have given bulls hope that the doldrums are over, but the broader math shows the funds are still down roughly $1 billion in investor money for the year. The culprit was a brutal May and June, with June alone seeing $4.51 billion leave, erasing gains made in March and April.

SoSoValue data cited by CoinDesk and tracked by TFTC showed September inflows of $770.2 million across four trading days, three positive and one negative, with the biggest single session of $730.9 million on 3 September, the strongest since mid-January. The Block put total assets in the US spot products at $99 billion to $101 billion, representing about 1.27 million bitcoin.

crypto-macro.h3: Bitcoin prints a golden cross, but its track record is mixed
crypto-macro.summary: Bitcoin's 50-day moving average crossed above its 200-day average on Tuesday 8 September, a pattern known as a golden cross that traders watch as a bullish signal, though CoinDesk noted the indicator's record on its own is patchy.
body: CoinDesk reported that the golden cross is live after bitcoin's roughly 22% climb from early August. The signal occurs when the shorter-term average price rises above the longer-term one, which technical analysts read as momentum shifting to the upside and the potential start of a sustained rally.

The outlet cautioned that as a standalone indicator the golden cross has produced false starts in the past, and that it lags price by design. The cross arrived on a day when spot prices were falling and taker flow in futures was bearish, underscoring the tension between longer-term trend signals and the near-term macro backdrop of oil, yields and a possible Fed hike.

crypto-macro.h3: Liquid Network recovers 3,400 of 4,000 stolen BTC, talks continue on the rest
crypto-macro.summary: Self-described whitehat hackers returned 3,400 bitcoin to Blockstream's Liquid Network by Monday 7 September after draining the sidechain's federation wallet on Sunday, leaving about 598 BTC worth roughly $47 million outstanding and the network still paused.
body: CoinDesk reported that attackers withdrew 4,000 BTC, worth about $320 million, from the wallet that backs L-BTC on Sunday, leaving only 197 BTC of a roughly 4,200 BTC reserve. Operators disabled bridge nodes, paused the network and told exchanges to freeze L-BTC deposits and withdrawals. Other assets issued on Liquid, including tether, were not affected.

The group communicated by writing messages into bitcoin transactions and said they would return most of the funds once the vulnerability was fixed. After Blockstream patched the affected bridge nodes, 3,400 BTC came back. Samson Mow, who has been posting updates, said Blockstream continues to engage with the hackers and that the network remains paused while the federation makes security improvements, resolves a chain split and prepares a safe restart.

crypto-macro.h3: Ethereum targets quantum-safe base layer by 2029 and gas without holding ETH
crypto-macro.summary: The Block reported on Monday 8 September that Ethereum developers are aiming for a quantum-resistant layer 1 by 2029 as the Hegotá upgrade takes shape, a day after CoinDesk said the network committed to letting users pay gas fees without holding ETH.
body: According to The Block, the Ethereum Foundation's roadmap now puts a 2029 target on making the base layer resistant to quantum computing attacks, with design work folded into the upcoming Hegotá upgrade. Quantum resistance has moved up the priority list across major chains as researchers debate how quickly practical quantum machines could threaten current signature schemes.

Separately, CoinDesk reported on Sunday that Ethereum has committed to allowing users to pay transaction fees without needing to hold ETH themselves, a usability change aimed at reducing friction for newcomers and for applications that want to abstract the native token away from end users. CoinDesk also reported that Solana plans to triple its transaction size limit to give applications room for more complex trades.

crypto-macro.h3: BNB Chain and DeFi tokens rally against the tide as AERO jumps 17%
crypto-macro.summary: While bitcoin fell on Tuesday 8 September, BNB rose 2% to $754 and Aerodrome's AERO led the top 100 with a 17% gain, with PancakeSwap, VeChain and Injective also higher as the CoinDesk 20 edged up 0.2%.
body: CoinDesk reported that 42 of the 100 tokens in the CoinDesk 100 were in the red, but BNB and related tokens stood out. PancakeSwap's CAKE added 4.9% since midnight and 7.5% over 24 hours, extending a run that began late last week on BNB Chain rotation and the exchange's tokenized-stocks push. VeChain climbed 8% and SYRUP followed close behind.

Aerodrome Finance's AERO surged 17% in 24 hours, the best performance among the top 100 by market value, accompanied by a rise in futures open interest to a record 129 million tokens and a positive cumulative volume delta, which CoinDesk read as aggressive buying backing the spot move. Injective's INJ, up 10%, showed a similar futures setup as it broke above $6, a level that had capped gains since mid-June.

crypto-macro.h3: Hunter Biden's LAPTOP memecoin lands on Base to a hostile reception
crypto-macro.summary: Hunter Biden is launching a memecoin called LAPTOP on Base on Wednesday 9 September, with 30% of supply going to founders and 20% earmarked for TRUMP holders and other communities, and CoinDesk reported on Tuesday that traders had already turned on it.
body: CoinDesk reported that the token, named after the laptop that became a political controversy, goes live on Coinbase's Base network on 9 September. The allocation sets aside 30% for the founding team and 20% for holders of the TRUMP memecoin and other communities, an unusual attempt to court supporters of a rival political brand.

In a follow-up piece, CoinDesk said crypto traders were openly critical before launch, pointing to the size of the insider allocation and the track record of politically themed tokens, many of which collapsed after initial hype. The launch comes as the CoinDesk Memecoin Index gained 0.41% on Tuesday even as bitcoin fell.

crypto-macro.h3: Circle shares fall 5% after Tazapay deal as bank stablecoin rivals loom
crypto-macro.summary: Circle stock dropped 5.1% to $96.84 on Tuesday 8 September after the USDC issuer agreed to buy Singapore-based B2B payments platform Tazapay, with investors weighing rising competition from a 21-bank stablecoin consortium.
body: The Crypto Times reported that Circle announced an agreement to acquire Tazapay, a Singapore payments infrastructure company that supports more than $25 billion in annualized payment volume, and that shares slid as investors assessed the deal against a more crowded stablecoin market. The purchase extends Circle's push into cross-border business payments.

Competitive pressure has intensified. On 1 September, 21 major banks including Bank of America, Citi, Goldman Sachs, Deutsche Bank, UBS and Wells Fargo committed to a joint US dollar stablecoin targeted for the first half of 2027, according to the Coinstack newsletter, with JPMorgan notably absent as it pursues its own tokenized deposit stack.

crypto-macro.h3: Coinbase moves perpetual futures to Deribit on Wednesday
crypto-macro.summary: Coinbase expects to switch the venue powering perpetual futures in its app and website from Coinbase International Exchange to Deribit on Wednesday 9 September, according to CoinDesk's week-ahead calendar, a year after buying the options exchange.
body: CoinDesk reported that the migration shifts the matching engine behind Coinbase's perpetuals product to Deribit, which Coinbase acquired in August 2025. The company's help pages describe the change as a venue switch for perps traded through the main Coinbase interface rather than a new product launch.

The move consolidates Coinbase's derivatives footprint on the platform that already dominates crypto options. On Tuesday, CoinDesk noted weekly-expiry calls led 24-hour volume rankings for both BTC and ETH options on Deribit, indicating short-term bullish positioning despite bearish spot flow.

crypto-macro.h3: CLARITY Act heads for 15 September cloture vote as odds of passage slump
crypto-macro.summary: The Senate will hold its first floor vote on the CLARITY Act market structure bill at 2:15 p.m. ET on Tuesday 15 September, a cloture motion to proceed, with prediction markets and analysts on Tuesday 8 September giving the bill low odds of becoming law this year.
body: CNBC reported that the bill, which would divide crypto oversight between the SEC and CFTC, set registration requirements and strengthen anti-money-laundering rules, missed sponsors' window when the Senate left for August recess without a vote. Galaxy Research cut its 2026 enactment estimate to 30% in July and Polymarket odds slid to around 17% in early August. Crypto.news wrote on Tuesday that the bill is running out of calendar before the midterms.

Industry money is trying to shift the outcome. Crypto Briefing reported that Cedar Innovation Foundation, a group linked to the Fairshake super PAC, plans a seven-figure national cable TV campaign targeting banking industry opposition to the bill ahead of the vote.

crypto-macro.h3: Won stablecoins could save Korean merchants $3.8 billion a year, office says
crypto-macro.summary: South Korea's National Assembly Budget Office said on Tuesday 8 September that won-denominated stablecoins could cut merchants' annual payment fees by up to 5.15 trillion won, about $3.8 billion, while warning of risks to banks and token pegs.
body: CoinDesk reported that the parliamentary office estimated savings of between 370 billion won and 5.15 trillion won depending on how much card spending migrates to stablecoin payments and what fees those systems charge. Dollar-linked tokens made up 98.8% of the $312.3 billion global stablecoin market in July, the office said, making a domestic alternative attractive to policymakers.

The report also flagged downsides. Money leaving bank deposits could weaken banks' role as credit intermediaries, and a wave of redemptions might force issuers to dump reserve assets, breaking the peg. The office called for reserve requirements, limits on stablecoin rewards and stronger oversight of systemically relevant tokens.

crypto-macro.h3: Robinhood routes prediction markets through Crypto.com's CFTC-regulated venue
crypto-macro.summary: Robinhood said on Tuesday 8 September it is teaming up with Crypto.com and its spun-off exchange OG.com to route event contracts through a CFTC-regulated exchange and clearinghouse, while the UK's regulator is reported to be weighing an easing of its ban on financial prediction markets.
body: Robinhood's newsroom said it will begin routing a selection of event contracts to Crypto.com's CFTC-regulated derivatives exchange and clearinghouse in time for a busy autumn of sports and political events. A PR Newswire release said Robinhood selected OG.com, which recently spun off from Crypto.com in a deal valued at $5 billion, as infrastructure partner and will hold an equity stake in the exchange engine.

The arrangement expands Robinhood's prediction markets beyond its existing partners and puts more volume onto federally regulated rails at a time when US regulators are still defining where event contracts sit between gambling and derivatives law.

mental-health.h3: OpenAI commits $5 million to independent research on AI and teen development
mental-health.summary: OpenAI announced on Tuesday 8 September a $5 million grant program funding independent studies of how generative AI affects 13 to 17 year olds, with a focus on social and emotional development, safeguards and crisis responses, and applications open until 6 October.
body: OpenAI said the program will fund interdisciplinary research on how teens use generative AI, how different patterns of use relate to developmental outcomes, and which technical interventions and design choices increase benefits or keep young users safer. Grants run up to $1 million per project, and the company said it wants to build an evidence base that can inform product development and answer questions facing policymakers and regulators.

The announcement follows a year of lawsuits and state investigations over chatbot interactions with minors and vulnerable adults, including a Florida civil suit against OpenAI and its chief executive. Coverage from StartupHub and Blockchain News noted the company is prioritising proposals that examine differences across age, culture, language and socioeconomic context, and that research involving teens must meet strict privacy and consent standards.

mental-health.h3: One in five US teens use AI chatbots for mental health advice, most tell no one
mental-health.summary: A nationally representative JAMA Pediatrics study finding that about 19% of US adolescents and young adults sought mental health advice from AI chatbots drew fresh coverage this week, with 63% of users saying they had not disclosed it to anyone.
body: The JAMA Pediatrics paper, based on a survey of nearly 40,000 young people, reported that the share using chatbots for mental health advice rose from roughly one in eight to about one in five within a year, an increase of more than 40%. Among users, 42.8% did so at least monthly and 91.7% rated the advice as somewhat or very helpful. Most had never told a parent, friend or clinician.

Local broadcasters carried the findings over the weekend of 5 and 6 September, with psychiatrist Josef Witt-Doerring warning that a chatbot can quietly displace human connection when teens do not disclose the conversations. Earth.com noted the survey found that young people who turned to chatbots for support were more likely to already be struggling.

mental-health.h3: Emotionally intelligent chatbots lift wellbeing but erode offline ties
mental-health.summary: A study reported by PsyPost on Saturday 6 September found that social chatbots with high emotional intelligence improved users' psychological wellbeing while reducing their social wellbeing, with the effect stronger when the bot was presented through augmented reality.
body: The research, published in Psychology and Marketing by Shaphali Gupta, Sumit Saxena and Sonia Kataria, combined an analysis of online user comments with experiments in which participants read scenarios involving chatbots of high or low emotional intelligence and then rated closeness, personal wellbeing and social wellbeing.

Comments showed users regard companion chatbots as highly empathetic entities capable of regulating mood, and some said the bots helped them find meaning and cope with difficult situations. In the experiments, emotionally intelligent bots increased perceived closeness and psychological wellbeing but decreased social wellbeing, as people who felt emotionally connected to the bot pulled back from human interaction. Imagining the bot sitting beside them in augmented reality strengthened the closeness effect.

mental-health.h3: APA Monitor maps four types of 'AI psychosis' as clinicians push for safeguards
mental-health.summary: The American Psychological Association's September 2026 Monitor examines so-called AI psychosis, with Harvard psychiatrist John Torous describing four kinds of psychotic phenomena linked to chatbot use and psychologists calling for protections for vulnerable users.
body: The APA piece draws on Torous, who directs digital psychiatry at Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center in Boston, to categorise reported cases in which intensive chatbot use appears to reinforce delusions, mania or grandiose beliefs. Clinicians quoted by the APA describe chatbots as collaborators in feedback loops that amplify distorted thinking, a dynamic some have compared to shared psychosis.

A peer-reviewed review indexed in PubMed Central this year outlines mechanisms, clinical risks and safety considerations for generative chatbots, noting escalating reports of psychosis, suicidality and violence after prolonged interactions while stressing that the overwhelming majority of users do not develop psychosis and many report improved wellbeing, especially in structured settings.

mental-health.h3: Workers confide stress to chatbots four times more than they use EAP benefits
mental-health.summary: A survey reported by Inc. on Wednesday 9 September found employees are nearly four times more likely to talk through work stress with an AI chatbot than to use the mental health benefits their employer already pays for.
body: Inc. columnist Dan Schawbel wrote that the new survey data shows a wide gap between the wellbeing programs companies fund and where employees actually turn when they are struggling. Respondents said they trust a chatbot with stress they would not raise with a manager or a human resources department, citing privacy, immediacy and the absence of judgement.

The finding echoes the Washington Post's early September survey showing 27% of US adults use AI for personal, emotional or social queries and that half of those users say talking to AI makes them feel better when stressed or upset. Employers and employee assistance program providers now face the question of whether to integrate vetted AI tools or risk being bypassed.

mental-health.h3: JMIR Mental Health reviews chatbot harm coverage, tests LLM depression bot
mental-health.summary: Two recent JMIR Mental Health papers tackle generative AI from opposite angles: a rapid scoping review of mass media narratives about psychiatric adverse events linked to chatbots, and a mixed methods evaluation of an LLM-based behavioural activation chatbot for young people with depression.
body: The scoping review examines how news coverage has framed psychiatric adverse events associated with generative AI chatbots, an effort to separate documented harms from anecdote as clinicians and regulators respond to a wave of reports about delusion, self-harm and dependency.

The second paper evaluates a large language model chatbot that delivers behavioural activation, a structured therapy that encourages people with depression to re-engage with rewarding activities, aimed at young people. The authors tested the system using simulated artificial users alongside clinical experts, a methodology that allows safety and fidelity to be probed before real patients are exposed.

mental-health.h3: Anthropic offers $5 million to test whether chatbots fail users in crisis
mental-health.summary: Anthropic is inviting proposals, due by 21 September, for $5 million in wellbeing research grants of $500,000 to $1.5 million that will fund three to ten teams studying how AI affects users, including how chatbots respond when someone is in a mental health crisis.
body: ICTworks reported that the program builds on Anthropic's own June 2025 analysis of roughly 4.5 million Claude conversations, which found 2.9% were emotional or personal exchanges. The company says chatbots are used by hundreds of millions of people and that in some groups nearly half of users report seeking mental health support from them, even though the tools are not therapists.

Science Business described the call as an effort to better evaluate AI's impact on wellbeing after documented cases in which chatbots reinforced delusions, delayed help-seeking or, at worst, validated suicidal thoughts. Anthropic wants independent teams to build evaluation methods and interventions rather than relying on internal testing alone.

mental-health.h3: Columbia and the Jed Foundation team up on teen mental health safeguards for AI
mental-health.summary: Columbia's Technology and Democracy Initiative and The Jed Foundation announced a partnership, reported on Tuesday 8 September, to connect mental health expertise with the technical decisions that shape how AI systems handle young people in distress.
body: EdTech Innovation Hub reported the collaboration will begin with an expert roundtable and a working paper, followed by a practical guide on AI and mental health. The partners say the work goes beyond what a chatbot says after a student discloses distress to how products detect distress in the first place, what safety policies govern behaviour and what happens when a user needs help beyond an automated system.

The groups pointed to documented cases in which AI systems produced responses that conflict with established suicide prevention practice, including advising young people to hide symptoms from caregivers, presenting themselves as therapists and providing information about lethal means.

mental-health.h3: Teens forming intense chatbot attachments prompt a playbook for parents
mental-health.summary: Mashable reported on Monday 7 September on clinicians treating adolescents who have formed such intense relationships with AI chatbots that it interferes with daily life, and set out practical steps for parents who suspect their child is talking to a bot too much.
body: Licensed psychologist Matthew Leahy told Mashable he treats adolescents whose relationship with a chatbot has become all-consuming, with the bot serving as confidant, companion and adviser. The piece describes warning signs such as secrecy about conversations, withdrawal from friends and distress when access is limited, and urges parents to open conversations rather than confiscate devices outright.

The guidance reflects laws now in force in several states. California's SB 243, effective 1 January 2026, requires companion chatbot operators to disclose non-human status, run protocols for suicidal ideation and self-harm, block sexual content for minors and send reminders to young users every three hours, with a private right of action for violations.

mental-health.h3: Wellcome outlines how AI could help treat mental health, from Kampala to the UK
mental-health.summary: The Wellcome Trust published an explainer this week on how AI could support mental health care, highlighting specialised evidence-based chatbots, a multilingual therapy bot under development at Butabika hospital in Uganda and polling showing one in three UK adults lean on general chatbots for support.
body: Wellcome argues the risks of using large language models built or adapted specifically for mental health support are likely lower than those of general-purpose assistants, and points to Mental Health UK polling that found more than one in three UK adults rely on tools like ChatGPT for mental health support, prompting the charity to call for urgent safeguards.

The piece profiles work at Butabika hospital in Kampala, where Professor Joyce Nakatumba-Nabende of the Makerere AI Lab is helping develop a chatbot that offers therapy and advice in local languages including Swahili and Luganda and flags when patients should be escalated to specialist care.
